marketInsightsHtml:
La charge de base Day-Ahead allemande et néerlandaise a augmenté de 66,00 € pour s'établir à 315,00 €/MWh, la charge de base Day-Ahead française a bondi de 31,00 € à 270,00 €/MWh, et la charge de base Day-Ahead britannique a augmenté de 34,60 £ à 213,60 £/MWh. Sur l'ensemble des courbes, le 26 novembre allemand a grimpé de 7,65 € à 229,35 €/MWh, le novembre français a gagné 8,25 € à 219,00 €/MWh et le novembre britannique a augmenté de 7,00 £ à 198,00 £/MWh.

L'indisponibilité du nucléaire français en novembre est prévue à 14,1 GW, les faibles débits du Rhône incitant EDF à alerter à partir de dimanche sur d'éventuelles limites de production à Saint-Alban.

marketInsights.gas:
European natural gas staged a major breakout on Wednesday, with the Dutch TTF front-month breaching the €100/MWh threshold for the first time since December 2022 to settle up €4.48 at €100.30/MWh, while Day-Ahead jumped €5.15 to €102.35/MWh. This morning, prices have seen modest profit-taking, consolidating around €97.50–€98.00/MWh. In the UK, NBP surged in tandem, Day-Ahead broke 250p/th for the first time in nearly four years to settle up 12.44p at 249.99p/th, while November 26 added 10.84p to 247.54p/th.

The rally was triggered by heightened geopolitical friction after reports emerged that Washington had urged Gulf allies to prepare for potential military strikes against Iran following next week's US midterm elections, overshadowing earlier diplomatic talks in Tehran. Physical transit through the Strait of Hormuz remains heavily compromised, with QatarEnergy officially extending its force majeure on Edison’s 6.4 bcm/yr contract through to 30 December. Severe industrial demand destruction is setting in: European fertilizer major Yara reported peak gas costs and confirmed it is running maximum quarterly ammonia curtailments of 270,000 tonnes, replacing domestic synthesis with imported product. Meanwhile, the TTF Summer '28 vs Winter '28 spread inverted to a record -€1.09/MWh, highlighting persistent structural refill concerns well beyond current EU mandates. Domestically, the BBL interconnector completed its physical flow reversal towards Great Britain today, providing vital import deliverability.

Prompt supply is further squeezed by extended unplanned Norwegian outages across Karstø, Oseberg, Kollsnes, and Åsgard. EU storage sits at 74.96% capacity (849.1 TWh), the lowest late October level on record since 2009, with Germany lagging at 61.73%, the Netherlands at 65.61%, and the UK holding 41.31%.

While mild conditions linger today, an expansive blocking high pressure will draw cold easterly air and sub-normal temperatures across Central and Western Europe from Friday into next week, with forecasters noting a 65% risk of Sudden Stratospheric Warming.
marketInsights.power:
European prompt power markets surged on Wednesday as climbing gas costs collided with an imminent renewable collapse. German and Dutch Day-Ahead baseload spiked by €66.00 to settle at €315.00/MWh, French Day-Ahead jumped €31.00 to €270.00/MWh, and UK Day-Ahead rallied £34.60 to £213.60/MWh. Across the curves, German November 26 climbed €7.65 to €229.35/MWh, French November gained €8.25 to €219.00/MWh, and UK November rose £7.00 to £198.00/MWh. German Calendar 2027 advanced €4.10 to a record €160.35/MWh, widening its premium over 2028 to a fresh high of €43.55/MWh.

Renewable generation is set to bottom out as high pressure centers over the UK and Northwest Europe. German wind output is forecast to plunge to 2.8–3.5 GW through Saturday, UK wind drops below 4.5 GW today and averages below 5.5 GW into early November, and Dutch wind was revised down to 1.5 GW.

Generation margins remain tight amid widespread nuclear and hydro constraints. French November nuclear unavailability is scheduled at 14.1 GW, with low Rhône river flows prompting EDF to warn of potential generation limits at Saint-Alban starting Sunday. In the UK, Drax declared its 645 MW biomass unit 2 unavailable across Q1 2027, reducing non-interconnector winter capacity. In the Alpine and Nordic regions, severe hydrological deficits persist. Swiss hydro stocks widened their deficit to long-term norms to 12.5 percentage points, while Nordic hydro reserves trail the five-year average by 10.3 TWh, prompting generators to conserve water.

Merit-order economics remain overwhelmingly tilted toward coal over gas, with German November 40% coal dark spreads widening their advantage over clean sparks to €93.31/MWh (€105.08/MWh dark vs. €11.77/MWh spark), keeping coal running at maximum capacity.
